own_scenes.desc: Desde Rakim, KRS-One y Kane, la lírica es un arte competitivo: unos escriben en libretas, otros en el móvil en un atasco, otros, como Biggie, Jay-Z o Styles P, en la cabeza. Para unos hay que «dejar joyas» y enseñar (Chuck D: «no rimo por rimar»); para otros basta con que suene bien sobre la base. Cormega tira nueve de cada diez rimas; K-Rino dice que el bloqueo es falta de lecturas; Bruce Lee y las diez mil horas. El negro (ghostwriting) existe desde que Caz rapeó sin saberlo en «Rapper’s Delight»: Kane escribía para la Juice Crew, The D.O.C. y Eminem para Dr. Dre, y Meek Mill acusó a Drake; para unos traiciona la autenticidad, para otros es como Al Pacino haciendo de cubano.

refs.q: You fear the man that’s done one kick ten thousand times.
refs.para: I’ve studied the storytellers in this music, from Slick Rick to Ghostface [Killah] and really just honed my own style. It’s very much like martial arts, like the old Bruce Lee saying: “You don’t fear the man that’s done ten thousand kicks once. You fear the man that’s done one kick ten thousand times.” Even though verses aren’t all the same, it’s the fact that you put that time in to put so many verses in.
refs.chapter: Cap. 21: Take It and Flip It

refs.q: Rock the mic, spit game, tell the truth as I see it, don’t pull no punches.
refs.para: Ice Cube (artist, N.W.A): When I heard the line “I don’t rhyme for the sake of riddlin’ ” from Chuck D, now that line sticks with me, because to me it’s like, “You got the mic. Rock the mic, but man, give us a little bit of medicine. Drop some jewels on us. You an MC. You’re supposed to be spitting game or letting us know what time it is.” I’ve always had that mentality that that’s the mission: Rock the mic, spit game, tell the truth as I see it, don’t pull no punches. That, to me, is what I’m supposed to be doing.
refs.chapter: Cap. 21: Take It and Flip It

refs.q: Knowing when it’s not the shit is where it’s at.
refs.para: The D.O.C. (artist, Dallas): I don’t know how I know it, but I know it. I think anybody that raps knows it. The difference is being able to know when it’s not the shit. Knowing when it’s the shit is easy. Knowing when it’s not the shit is where it’s at. You have to listen with your ears and not your emotions.
refs.chapter: Cap. 21: Take It and Flip It
